Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR routes session consumers through actor-owned memory storage while leaving production incognito acquisition on its existing owner. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Useful maintainer-directed preparation, but an unresolved authority defect and absent final-effect authority evidence prevent merge readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Product **Kind:** Refactor · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Incognito consumers still depend on separate storage paths that must be adapted before the planned memory-owner cutover. **Reason:** The maintainer has selected this staged direction, and production activation remains deferred. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 6 items remain** Keep this maintainer-directed refactor open; the prior ACP caller-guard defect remains in the reviewed head. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Authority-chain proof required: show administrator access allowed and non-administrator access denied through the changed memory-backed Gateway and MCP consumers, then revoke caller authority or reparent the completion source after preparation and show rejection before disclosure, mutation, or tool I/O. The complete body supplies owner tests and prior-head workload/update receipts, but no trace of these final effects; preserve the inactive backend and redact credentials, IPs, phone numbers, and private endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Preserve the ACP caller guard through memory metadata writes (P2)** - With a live memory binding for agent:main:dashboard:incognito-acp, passing assertCommitAllowed that throws should reject the write, but this callback is only invoked for stage === "transaction". Memory snapshots and session.entry.patch authorize at "commit", so the callback never runs; prepareAcpSessionMutation and commitAcpSessionMutation also receive assertCurrent that checks only the actor and binding authority. Consequently, a cancelled or superseded ACP caller can still patch the entry and persist runtime metadata. Compose caller liveness into the actual entry and shared-worker effect guards, keeping it separate from metadata views intentionally invalidated during publication. This is the unresolved prior finding. - [ ] **Resolve security concern: Caller-operation authority is not preserved** - The session actor may remain live after the ACP manager operation is cancelled or superseded; actor liveness therefore cannot replace the manager's independent authorization guard. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk** - Prepared memory-backed Gateway and MCP authority must be shown to reject revoked administrator access and reparented completion sources before disclosure, mutation, or tool I/O. - [ ] **Improve patch quality** - Add final-effect proof for non-administrator access and for caller revocation or completion-source reparenting before disclosure, mutation, or tool I/O. - [ ] **Explain or restore the original intent of ACP shared-worker mutation authority** - 05161b949bcded143f477df59834b831054f555e: Move ACP metadata work to the shared worker while preserving lifecycle ownership and live request authority, as described in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167086. ## Findings - [P2] Preserve the ACP caller guard through memory metadata writes — `src/acp/runtime/session-meta-memory.ts:78-80` - [medium] Caller-operation authority is not preserved — `src/acp/runtime/session-meta-memory.ts:78` ### Provenance - `ACP shared-worker mutation authority` changes intended behavior without addressing why it exists (05161b949bcded143f477df59834b831054f555e: Move ACP metadata work to the shared worker while preserving lifecycle ownership and live request authority, as described in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167086.) ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Supply a production-owner trace of allowed and forbidden memory-backed effects, including caller revocation and completion-source reparenting; the supplied tests do not establish this final-effect scenario.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Gateway, agent, ACP, and SDK consumers send session operations to the selected actor; memory state stays process-local, while shared ACP runtime metadata still uses the durable worker. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Gateway and agent consumers] --> B[Selected session binding] B --> C[Existing production incognito owner] B --> D[Inactive memory actor] D --> E[Process-local session state] D --> F[Shared ACP metadata worker] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Preserve ACP caller authority through both storage owners and keep the memory backend inactive until its final-effect authority contract is demonstrated. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source establishes a deterministic case: with a live memory binding, an assertCommitAllowed callback that throws is never invoked by the new ACP adapter, allowing its entry and metadata mutations to proceed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The staged adapter approach follows the existing actor direction, but caller liveness must be composed into actual effect checks rather than attached to an admission stage the operation never uses. Full review comments: - [P2] Preserve the ACP caller guard through memory metadata writes — `src/acp/runtime/session-meta-memory.ts:78-80` With a live memory binding for agent:main:dashboard:incognito-acp, passing assertCommitAllowed that throws should reject the write, but this callback is only invoked for stage === "transaction". Memory snapshots and session.entry.patch authorize at "commit", so the callback never runs; prepareAcpSessionMutation and commitAcpSessionMutation also receive assertCurrent that checks only the actor and binding authority. Consequently, a cancelled or superseded ACP caller can still patch the entry and persist runtime metadata. Compose caller liveness into the actual entry and shared-worker effect guards, keeping it separate from metadata views intentionally invalidated during publication. This is the unresolved prior finding. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.92 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [653b1d8bba92](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/653b1d8bba921c00b241938e35852afd724c6723). ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Hold for authority validation (recommended)** Keep this PR open and inactive while the ACP guard is repaired and allowed, forbidden, and revoked authority is exercised through the changed final-effect consumers. ### Provenance checked - `Inactive memory actor and deferred production acquisition` keeps the original intent (5bd4f88535c66197b6d07442b82f7f68d94be6fa: Provide the memory backend while retaining the existing production incognito owner until the coordinated cutover.) - `Detached transcript snapshot projection` keeps the original intent (320d57bd4fb1280e23f4fb87cdd420751ca14828: Project actor-owned transcript snapshots without reopening their physical store; the changed adapter retains checks before observer disclosure and final result return.) - `Materialized wrapper dependency context` keeps the original intent (7f2637f18d79c0a74e414da629062f65064d1ff4: Pin wrapper dependencies to their installed package directories; the patch extends that closure while retaining manifest-version checks.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security Needs attention: The memory ACP adapter loses caller-operation authority, and changed disclosure and completion paths need final-effect validation. ### Evidence Security concerns: - [medium] Caller-operation authority is not preserved — `src/acp/runtime/session-meta-memory.ts:78` The session actor may remain live after the ACP manager operation is cancelled or superseded; actor liveness therefore cannot replace the manager's independent authorization guard. Confidence: 0.99 What I checked: - **Introduced ACP caller guard is unreachable:** The new adapter places assertCommitAllowed inside a transaction-stage authorize callback, but snapshot and entry-patch operations use commit-stage authorization; its shared worker assertions also omit the caller guard. ([`src/acp/runtime/session-meta-memory.ts:78`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be/src/acp/runtime/session-meta-memory.ts#L78), [c250a71bf8b9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be)) - **Actual storage admission stage:** Memory storage checks the authoritative preimage with authorize("commit"), establishing why the adapter's transaction-only guard does not run. ([`src/config/sessions/session-actor-memory-storage.ts:106`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be/src/config/sessions/session-actor-memory-storage.ts#L106), [c250a71bf8b9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be)) - **Caller guard carries real lifecycle authority:** The ACP manager composes caller authorization and current-manager-actor checks into assertCommitAllowed; checking only the session storage binding does not preserve this contract. ([`src/acp/control-plane/manager.core.ts:609`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be/src/acp/control-plane/manager.core.ts#L609), [c250a71bf8b9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be)) - **Prior finding remains unchanged:** The ACP memory adapter is unchanged from the previously reviewed head, so the existing finding remains unresolved rather than being a newly discovered concern. ([`src/acp/runtime/session-meta-memory.ts:78`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be/src/acp/runtime/session-meta-memory.ts#L78), [c250a71bf8b9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be)) - **Production cutover remains deferred:** Current main selects native-incognito acquisition for ordinary incognito input, and the reviewed exclusion test expects no memory owner to be created. ([`src/config/sessions/session-input-actor.ts:87`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/653b1d8bba921c00b241938e35852afd724c6723/src/config/sessions/session-input-actor.ts#L87), [653b1d8bba92](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/653b1d8bba921c00b241938e35852afd724c6723)) - **Maintainer direction and supplied proof:** The complete REST body describes an inactive staged cutover, explicitly accepts append-order, expiry, search, and close-settlement tradeoffs, and supplies test, benchmark, and prior-head update receipts; it supplies no allowed/forbidden final-effect authority trace. ([c250a71bf8b9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/c250a71bf8b954b978de365b18f6b21a2c8a34be)) ### PR surface PR surface statistics unavailable: the file list is incomplete. ### Labels Label changes: No label changes.
